canonical_record.label: GRACE groundwater inference requires subtraction of other water stores
canonical_record.summary: Scanlon and colleagues describe deriving groundwater storage changes from GRACE total water storage by subtracting snow, reservoir surface-water and modeled soil-moisture storage changes.

sources.title: Groundwater depletion and sustainability of irrigation in the US High Plains and Central Valley

statement: Scanlon and colleagues describe deriving groundwater storage changes from GRACE total water storage by subtracting snow, reservoir surface-water and modeled soil-moisture storage changes.

scope.assumptions: Snow storage, reservoir storage and soil-moisture estimates from additional monitoring or models
scope.limitations: GRACE does not independently measure groundwater alone; subtraction uncertainty remains.

support.quote: GRACE measures changes in total water storage, which are used to estimate changes in groundwater storage (GWS) by subtracting changes in storage in snow (snow water equivalent) from the Snow Data Assimilation System, surface water from reservoir monitoring, and soil moisture derived from Global Land Data Assimilation System models

canonical_record.label: JPL GRACE mascon native and mapped grid distinction
canonical_record.summary: NASA JPL describes its GRACE/GRACE-FO RL06M v02 solution as 4,551 relatively independent surface-mass estimates derived using an equal-area 3-degree mascon grid, subsequently mapped onto a 0.5-degree latitude-longitude grid.

sources.title: JPL GRACE and GRACE-FO Mascon RL06M version 02 Datasets Released

statement: NASA JPL describes its GRACE/GRACE-FO RL06M v02 solution as 4,551 relatively independent surface-mass estimates derived using an equal-area 3-degree mascon grid, subsequently mapped onto a 0.5-degree latitude-longitude grid.

scope.population: JPL GRACE/GRACE-FO RL06M v02 mascon product
scope.assumptions: Mass-inversion solution mapped to a finer regular grid
scope.limitations: A 0.5-degree output grid does not imply independent 0.5-degree spatial resolving power.

support.quote: The complete Mascon solution consists of 4,551 relatively independent estimates of surface mass change that have been derived using an equal-area 3-degree grid of individual mascons. The final solutions are then mapped into 0.5-degree regular lat-lon grid.

canonical_record.label: Central Valley Hydrologic Model version 2 simulation period
canonical_record.summary: USGS describes Central Valley Hydrologic Model version 2 as using MODFLOW-OWHM to simulate groundwater and surface-water flow, irrigation, land subsidence and associated processes monthly from April 1961 through September 2019.

sources.title: MODFLOW-OWHM Used to Characterize the Groundwater Flow System of the Central Valley

statement: USGS describes Central Valley Hydrologic Model version 2 as using MODFLOW-OWHM to simulate groundwater and surface-water flow, irrigation, land subsidence and associated processes monthly from April 1961 through September 2019.

scope.limitations: Simulation and observational calibration do not automatically establish independent corroboration of GRACE groundwater estimates.

support.quote: In addition, the model utilizes a specialized version of MODFLOW called the MODFLOW-One-Water Hydrologic Flow Model (MODFLOW-OWHM) to simulate groundwater and surface-water flow, irrigated agriculture, land subsidence, and other key processes in the Central Valley monthly for April 1961 through September 2019.

canonical_record.label: Bayesian joint inference from GRACE and High Plains groundwater wells
canonical_record.summary: Pakrashi, Haran and Zuidema describe combining GRACE satellite measurements, groundwater-well observations and covariates using a Bayesian hierarchical framework to estimate High Plains groundwater variations over 2002–2022.

sources.title: Estimating water levels in the High Plains Aquifer by synthesizing satellite data with groundwater well observations

statement: Pakrashi, Haran and Zuidema describe combining GRACE satellite measurements, groundwater-well observations and covariates using a Bayesian hierarchical framework to estimate High Plains groundwater variations over 2002–2022.

scope.population: High Plains aquifer; GRACE and NGWMN observations
scope.assumptions: Bayesian hierarchical model jointly incorporating satellite, well and covariate data
scope.uncertainty: Numerical validation uncertainties not provided in retained abstract
scope.limitations: Joint data assimilation does not serve as an independent test of satellite-well agreement. Retained source is a preprint abstract.

support.quote: In this paper, we develop a downscaling framework for the satellite data that integrates the two sources and covariates using a Bayesian hierarchical framework.
Our approach yields high-resolution estimates of groundwater variations across the HPA from 2002--2022.
